items.author: szmyty
items.body:
**Qualified repair:** PRs #69–#72 are merged; actual repair qualification is exact source `4699235e9e925b76ca492d5a00a375ed37fb338e`, with [criterion-level proof](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/6f7edf957db630f7662254decbac18aae73a870a/audits/qualification-4699235.md) and [immutable review evidence](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/tree/eb92598f3a4a0dc426749c290bacfe7251452909). The original reproduction/recovery below is retained as history.

A fresh-output local ACT run leaves generated frontend assets unusable by the normal checkout owner. This was reproduced during the audit in #67; the six ACT jobs themselves passed. This is a developer-workflow defect, separate from the remaining hosted/device gates in #46. Closed #61 is provenance.

### Reproduction and evidence

Exact clean source: `cf12abe6c620dcbea3b806d1aa63a4715adea26a`, tree `d24d5435af64400da8bb665714b908cbbe638f7c`.
Linux x86_64 host UID/GID1000, Node24.19.0/npm11.9.0, ACT0.2.97; Ubuntu24 runner digest `19619a010b204f44c5340bff7d39b68551109fe6a56a53f75201ea91e05d4270`.

1. Start with the generated, ignored `steamdeck/decky/dist` absent, as on a fresh checkout. The audit verified no tracked paths, preserved the existing output and recorded its ownership/hashes.
2. Run the supported local candidate job (the actual reproduction used the full repeat six-job sequence):
   ```sh
   python3 scripts/local-ci.py candidate --act /workspace/.obsgod-tools/pkg/bin/act --state /workspace/.obsgod-tools/completion/act
   ```
3. ACT recreates `steamdeck/decky/dist` as UID/GID0, mode0755. Four JavaScript outputs are UID0/mode0644; the license file is UID1000. The checkout parent remains UID1000/mode0700.
4. As the normal UID1000 owner, run:
   ```sh
   npm --prefix steamdeck/decky run build
   ```
   Actual exit1:
   ```text
   Error: EACCES: permission denied, open 'dist/decky-api.js'
   at .../steamdeck/decky/rollup.config.js:15:1
   ```

Observed 2026-11-13T23:31:22.554027+00:00; failure-log SHA256 `42135c973f91e058d1f9ad30cd86d97f7b587a7d1990c242ae5c1614dae17ea4`. Source stayed clean/unchanged. The full ownership inventory, completed ACT receipts and failure/recovery logs are retained in the [audit packet](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/d6f67159fb88e664a4dad2e57950c29c0407653f/audits/local-act-2026-11-13.md) at evidence-only commit `d6f67159fb88e664a4dad2e57950c29c0407653f`.

### Expected behavior

A documented ACT run should leave generated frontend outputs usable by the ordinary checkout owner, including when the generated directory initially does not exist.

### Safe recovery observed

An attempted cross-parent move of the root-owned directory failed with EACCES without changing files. A same-parent rename to the absent, already-ignored `steamdeck/decky/.local-ci` preserved the exact output; a new UID1000 build then passed. No sudo/chown/chmod was used. All14 root candidate/audit hashes stayed unchanged. This is a bounded recovery workaround, not a fix.

### Acceptance

- [x] ACT followed by normal-host frontend typecheck/test/build passes from both initially absent and reused generated output, without manual privileged repair or renaming.
- [x] Preserve actual execution identities/provenance; choose bounded build identity or output isolation rather than recursively changing checkout ownership.
- [x] If cleanup is needed, verify safe non-symlink generated paths and preserve existing outputs; refuse unsafe/foreign paths.
- [x] Preserve production root guards and the nonroot installer/browser fixtures.
- [x] Retain exact repaired revision, ACT/host commands, ownership before/after, raw results and source/artifact-preservation evidence.

No duplicate billing, Dependency graph, physical Deck, provider, or publication scope is added here.

## Game capture observer disables a microphone enabled through the mixer

Evidence level: confirmed source and reproduced with external Go overlay / loopback OBS fixture.

Impact: sceneVideoWhitelist consults Settings.Microphone instead of the effective mixer preference and removes MicAudio from the keep set. The watcher disables the microphone scene item in IdleScene and GameScene while mixer preferences/source mute can still report microphone enabled/unmuted. Broadcasts, recordings and replay can silently lose microphone audio on game transitions. The reproduction starts with enabled scene items, retains microphone_enabled=true, and observes both scene items disabled.

Bounded repair: Resolve effective microphone policy once for a managed video cycle using the same mixer preference source as audio configuration, then preserve its scene membership through idle/game whitelist operations. Keep enable, mute and push-to-talk semantics distinct. Avoid another microphone preference store. Consolidating the effective-policy read is a bounded refactor tied to this defect.

items.author: szmyty
items.body:
## Completed

Merged in [PR #118](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/pull/118) at `852320741d3f23aa513e3798528b3576b8b179fb`. [Criterion-level review](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/852320741d3f23aa513e3798528b3576b8b179fb/docs/oss-experience-review.md) supports all 12 bounded OSS criteria. The owner explicitly moved migration before manual testing on 2026-11-22; [recorded amendment](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/blob/852320741d3f23aa513e3798528b3576b8b179fb/DECISIONS.md#owner-sequence-update-2026-11-22) supersedes the earlier sequence below. No runtime/device/service/rights/migration/release criterion was passed by this documentation merge.

---

Parent roadmap: #46. Requested follow-up: make deckystream easier to understand, try, troubleshoot and contribute to before its fresh-repository launch.

## Outcome and boundary

Deliver one coherent public OSS experience around the existing plugin and reusable CLI: readable repository presentation, task-oriented documentation, clear first-use/help routes, useful contributor intake and bounded repository hygiene.

This is a distinct polish issue, not a replacement for configuration #79, lifecycle #82, integration #83, qualification #85, actual Deck testing #86, migration #87, destination services #95, official install/v1 #88 or optional authentication research #89. Preserve all 230 original criteria/dependencies under #46. Its priority introduces no new hard prerequisite for the manual testing session.

Inspected baseline: default `master` at [f4561aaaf131b4bfe94d1aa02834890e8884a104](https://github.com/szmyty/obsgod/tree/f4561aaaf131b4bfe94d1aa02834890e8884a104). Current test candidate remains source `772230a` / immutable packet `430cc391`; editing documentation does not newly qualify that runtime.

## Demonstrated gaps and existing foundations

- More than 90 Markdown documents have no central `docs/README.md` navigation page.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md` gives policy links, but sends newcomers straight into long continuity/roadmap records without a short source map or docs/CLI/Decky starting routes.
- Issue forms offer only a Steam Deck bug report, despite the repository also exposing the reusable CLI.
- `docs/steam-deck-development.md` opens with the older Desktop-first installer journey and old #10 hardware tracking without a prominent historical label/current-install pointer.
- The README already has branding, feature explanations, preview limitations, installation steps, task links and optional support links. Refine these; do not recreate them or describe existing work as missing.
- `.github/FUNDING.yml` already drives GitHub funding and generated plugin support buttons. GitHub Sponsors, Buy Me a Coffee, Ko-fi, Open Collective and thanks.dev use the owner's existing handles. Patreon remains intentionally inactive in this repository; unconfigured cryptocurrency addresses remain hidden.

## Execution journey

1. **Map and reconcile.** Inventory public entry points, current versus historical guides, stale terminology, duplicated instructions, local links/anchors and generated versus authored material. Preserve immutable receipts, old downloads and the memorial.
2. **Polish the front door.** Make README routes obvious for a Steam Deck user, CLI user, contributor and someone needing help. Keep the selected aurora branding, readable light/dark presentation and honest preview status; distinguish required setup from optional tooling.
3. **Make documentation easy to follow.** Add a compact documentation index, improve headings/reading order and current-guide pointers, and walk the exact review-package → standard Decky installation → private setup → local picture/audio check → explicit Start → help route. Retain historical instructions as clearly labelled history.
4. **Improve contributor and repository hygiene.** Add a concise source map and docs/CLI/Decky contribution routes; review bug/feature intake, PR guidance, security/support/license links, source/generated-file ownership and naming consistency. Add or adjust only what demonstrably helps this project. Keep existing pinned tools; avoid generic policy/template inflation, mandatory new standards or a framework rewrite.
5. **Verify and hand off.** Review rendered pages and accessibility, changed links/anchors, cross-file consistency and deterministic support metadata. Record unresolved external destinations/owner facts separately. Keep later destination-specific URLs/settings with #87/#95 and final release acceptance with #88.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] **OSS-1:** README has directly labelled routes for Deck preview users, generic CLI users, contributors and help, with one clear current test download path.
- [x] **OSS-2:** A small central docs index groups current user tasks, contributor/architecture references, qualification records and historical material, linking canonical contracts rather than duplicating them.
- [x] **OSS-3:** Current entry pages consistently explain lowercase display name `deckystream`, compatible executable/plugin/storage names `obsgod`/`OBSGod`, the standard plugin ZIP and optional Desktop tools.
- [x] **OSS-4:** A newcomer can follow README → exact review packet/checksums → standard ZIP instructions → private setup/local clip → help without relying on an obsolete installer guide.
- [x] **OSS-5:** Instructions retain explicit Start, local sound/picture checks, separate-viewer confirmation, game-only video/audio limits and truthful preview/UNRUN qualifications. No fabricated CI, Store, release, rights or hardware-success badge/claim is added.
- [x] **OSS-6:** Historical guides touched by this work, including `docs/steam-deck-development.md`, have visible context/current-guide pointers while original facts, evidence and historical downloads remain intact.
- [x] **OSS-7:** CONTRIBUTING supplies docs, CLI and Decky starting routes with relevant source locations and existing focused-check commands, without requiring the full runtime matrix for prose-only edits.
- [x] **OSS-8:** Issue/PR intake covers the actual CLI and Deck audiences, directs private security concerns appropriately and asks for useful credential-safe reproductions without inventing contacts, response promises or mandatory accounts/services.
- [x] **OSS-9:** Existing support/security/license/attribution and repository navigation are coherent. Funding remains optional and derived from `.github/FUNDING.yml`; retain the existing inactive-Patreon/hidden-wallet decisions and make no payment/payout claim.
- [x] **OSS-10:** Reading order, descriptive headings/link labels, image alternatives, light/dark presentation and any demonstrated help/navigation wording gaps receive a bounded review. Any runtime/UI change gets its own affected checks and candidate handling; this is not a new UI redesign.
- [x] **OSS-11:** Record changed-link/anchor checks, rendered review and the four audience-route walkthroughs at the exact revision. Use existing pinned tooling where applicable; distinguish passed, failed, skipped, unavailable and unrun. No old runtime receipt is relabelled as new qualification.
- [x] **OSS-12:** Update continuity/current roadmap pointers and provide a concise before/after review record with remaining owner/destination facts. No extra child issues are required to close this bounded issue; existing acceptance owners remain unchanged.

## Sequence and closure

This work can proceed while waiting for access to the Steam Deck and alongside #85's remaining free-execution evidence. It must not delay or pretend to pass #86. After device fixes/acceptance, #87 performs only the specifically approved migration, #95 verifies actual destination services, and #88 binds the canonical new-install/v1 evidence. #46 reconciles last; #89 remains a separate design discussion.

No repository move, other-repository change, release publication, deployment, paid service, payment transaction or Store submission is authorized by this issue. Close it against the checklist and recorded review, not a merge alone.
